dataset.source_scope_note: Sessions are the pinned Coinbase 1h artifact aggregated to canonical UTC daily bars by the BTC-020 owner, and each session is decision-available at its own close boundary. BTC-019 has approved no canonical BTC reference, so every expectation below is scoped to this source: re-sourcing the fixture requires a fresh review, which the 2025-10 scenario exists to demonstrate.

scenarios.title: October 2023 reclaim: a trend still running when the window closed
review: Bitcoin spent six weeks between 26,500 and 28,300 after the August 2023 flush. The 16 October session opened the ETF-anticipation trend: a false approval headline printed 30,000 intraday and the session still closed at 28,520, back above the range.

The plan does not buy that spike. It waits for the first retest of the reclaimed 28,100-28,650 shelf and arms it on 19 October, with the 11 October low at 26,521 untested and higher lows at 28,083 and 28,122 behind it.

The 16 October breakout session's low, 27,135.92, is the structural invalidation: below it the reclaim did not happen. The 550-wide zone carries 275 of level noise, which binds over 0.3 x ATR20 in a quiet tape, so the stop sits at 26,860.92.
20 October opens at 28,734.51, above the zone, and trades down to 28,591.85. The zone is touched from above, so the entry references the zone's upper bound and not the session open.
23 October confirms the trend (+10.28%, 35,000 intraday). Its low, 29,890.89, is the first higher low worth trailing to, and the trail is taken on 24 October.

That trail is what authorises the second tranche: the stop moves from 26,860.92 to 29,563.60 on 1.117893 BTC, an improvement of 3,021.30 at the shared stop, so the 25 October add is not buying more of an unimproved risk.
27 October's 33,400 low is the next higher low. The 3 November trail moves the stop above the average entry, and the trade is still open when the window closes on 10 November.
expected_behaviour: the entry fills at the zone's upper bound, not at the 20 October open
two trail advances, each to a reviewed higher low, and the stop is never touched
the add fills above the running average entry, so the position never averages down
the position is marked at the last session rather than force closed, and its open accounting carries no R multiple because no closing fill exists

scenarios.title: 17 August 2023: the range break filled at the stop price, not a gap
review: From mid-July to mid-August 2023 Bitcoin held a 29,000-30,200 range on falling realized volatility; ATR20 was under 510 by 13 August, the quietest tape in this fixture.

The plan buys the range hold on 13 August in 29,100-29,350 with the 7 August low, 28,660.53, as invalidation. The quiet tape is what makes the stop tight: the buffer binds on 0.3 x ATR20 = 152.38 rather than on the zone's own 125 of noise, and the stop sits at 28,508.16.
14 August opens at 29,275.78, inside the zone, so the entry references the session open.
On 17 August the range broke: the session opened at 28,700.51 and traded to 25,234.76, -7.22%. The stop was inside that session's range.

The session opened above the stop, so the fill is at the stop price. A continuously traded 24/7 series has no session gap to open through, which is why a real stop-out here costs -1R plus slippage and fees and nothing more; the gapped-open path BTC-223 pins with constructed bars is not reachable on this data.
Price never returned to the entry inside the window: the 25 August close was 26,049.39.
expected_behaviour: one closed trade, stopped out on 17 August with STOP_TOUCHED and STOP_FILL_AT_STOP_PRICE
a realized R slightly worse than -1, entirely explained by the stop's own slippage and the two legs' fees
the maximum adverse excursion equals the trade's gross loss: the stop fill was the worst mark the position ever carried

scenarios.title: January 2024: a chased zone never touched, then a stop on the entry session
review: The US spot ETFs were approved on 10 January 2024 and listed on 11 January. The 11 January session printed 49,102.29 and closed at 46,342.66; 12 January fell 7.70%.

The first decision is the mistake the period is known for: arming a continuation zone at 47,800-48,600 under the launch high. Its one eligible session, 12 January, has a high of 46,522.20, below the zone, so the entry is terminally missed rather than chased on a later session, and it costs the account nothing.

The second decision buys the 22 January capitulation close, 39,524.27, with that session's own low, 39,372.44, as invalidation. Post-launch volatility had widened ATR20 to about 2,192, so the buffer binds on ATR and the stop sits at 38,714.96.

23 January opens at 39,524.27, inside the zone, and trades to 38,501. Entry and stop both belong to that one session, and the bracket authorised at the 22 January decision resolves the collision against the position: the entry fills, then the stop fills on the same session.
A trade that opens and closes inside one session leaves no excursion evidence, and BTC-165 reports MFE and MAE as absent rather than inventing an intrabar path.
expected_behaviour: the first entry is missed with ENTRY_ZONE_NOT_TOUCHED and ENTRY_DO_NOT_CHASE, and no notional, fee or ledger tranche exists for it
the second entry fills and is stopped out on its own entry session
the closed trade reports no MFE and no MAE

scenarios.title: February-March 2024: trimmed into the all-time high, then stopped
review: February 2024 was the first ETF-flow trend. Bitcoin left the 42,000-44,000 January range on 8-9 February and ran to the 73,835.57 all-time high on 14 March.

The plan arms the 48,300-49,300 shelf on 12 February with the 11 February low, 47,590.30, as invalidation. 13 February opens at 49,941.95, above the zone, and trades to 48,327.81: a zone-upper-bound fill at 49,324.65 against a 47,090.30 stop.
The 23 February low, 50,513.01, is the last higher low before the 26-28 February expansion (+5.42%, +4.66%, +9.53%). The 26 February trail lifts the stop to 50,001.75, above the entry.

11-12 March is the euphoria: 72,943.98 intraday, then a 68,603 washout inside two sessions. The 12 March decision reads euphoria as active with the hold score at 62 - above the 50 defensive band - so the trim is carried by the euphoria flag and not by the score band.
The 9 March low, 68,047.62, is the trailing structure taken on 13 March. The resulting 67,015.67 stop survives 14 March (low 68,454.47) and is taken out on 15 March (low 65,565.70).

The second trim, decided on 14 March, never executes. The stop resolves before the queued intent on 15 March, so the trim is refused as stale instead of being applied to a position that no longer exists.
expected_behaviour: one closed trade of about +8.5R, trimmed once and stopped out
the trim leaves the weighted average entry untouched, so the R denominator is still the risk taken at entry
the stop that fires first makes the queued second trim stale rather than executing it

known_composition_limit.description: The reviewed plan also added a second tranche on 27 February, after the 26 February trail improved the stop. That trade cannot currently be accounted: BTC-155 allocates a tranche quantity of notional/price that does not terminate in Decimal's 28-digit context, and BTC-165's pro-rata trim basis then misses the exact cash-flow identity by about 1e-23. BTC-223 recorded the same composition gap and left it to its owner, so the add is pinned here as a known limit on real history rather than quietly dropped from the review.

scenarios.title: 31 July 2024: the discretionary exit that beat the stop and missed the crash
review: The plan buys the 26 July reclaim (+3.24%, closing 67,924.08) in 66,600-68,000 with the 25 July low, 63,412.46, as invalidation. ATR20 was about 2,550, so the buffer binds on ATR and the stop sits at 62,647.43. The 27 July session opens inside the zone at 67,921.46.

The reclaim failed within three sessions: 29 July -2.16%, 30 July -0.90%, 31 July -2.36%. The 30 July decision reads the regime as invalidated with the hold score at 44 - above the 40 exit band - so the exit is carried by REGIME_INVALIDATION alone and not by a hold-score collapse.
The exit fills on 31 July at 66,136.60 for a 0.37R loss. The stop was still untouched: the 31 July low was 64,500.

The counterfactual is the point of the period. On 1 August the low was 62,212.81, so the stop would have filled at 62,616.10 for a full -1.006R before fees, 3,520.49 a coin worse than the exit; and the position would still have been open for the 5 August carry unwind, which opened at 58,131.31 and traded to 49,050.01, 25.8% below the exit.
expected_behaviour: one closed trade with exit reason REGIME_INVALIDATION, filled at the 31 July open less slippage
the standing stop is never touched before the exit
the exit price is better than the price the standing stop would have filled at on 1 August
the account carries no exposure through the 5 August capitulation

scenarios.title: 10 October 2025: a stop the pinned source touched and Bitstamp did not
review: The 10 October 2025 selloff is the event PRICE_SOURCE_POLICY_V1 uses to reject a single-venue reference: both validators touched a 107,270 stop that Bitstamp missed.

The plan buys the 1-6 October breakout on its first retest: zone 120,500-122,500 armed on 6 October with the 25 September low, 108,623.70, as invalidation. The 2,000-wide zone carries 1,000 of level noise, which binds over 0.3 x ATR20, so the stop sits at 107,623.70 - within 354 of the stop the BTC-019 study found source sensitive.
7 October opens at 124,723.57, above the zone, and trades to 120,636: a zone-upper fill at 122,561.25.
10 October opened at 121,714.51 and traded to 107,000 on this series. The stop is touched and fills at the stop price for -1.02R.
The stop was not a shakeout: the 17 October low, 103,516.75, is 3.8% below it, and the window closes with price under the stop.
expected_behaviour: one closed trade stopped out on 10 October at the stop price
a realized R of about -1.02, the stop's slippage and the two legs' fees beyond -1R
the expectation holds for the pinned source only: the recorded venue lows put the stop between what Bitstamp traded and what this series traded

source_sensitivity.note: The scenario's stop at 107,623.70 lies between the Bitstamp session low and the pinned Coinbase session low, so the same reviewed plan is stopped out on this source and on Bitfinex and is not stopped out on Bitstamp. BTC-019 remains in progress and no canonical reference is approved, so this scenario's expectation is explicitly source scoped.
